trials.notes: Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for a BODY fragment, walked tokens with next_token(), collected #text via get_modifiable_text(), and explicitly included opener-carried TITLE/TEXTAREA text while excluding SCRIPT/STYLE. All HTML API methods used are documented; execution passed 10/10 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

Same correct processor and token-walk pattern as the reference, with an additional harmless class_exists() guard. It used documented methods only: create_fragment(), next_token(), get_token_type(), get_token_name(), is_tag_closer(), and get_modifiable_text(). It handled decoded text and UTF-8 truncation; execution passed 10/10 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

Correct implementation and documented API use. The only minor idiom deduction is using get_tag() inside a next_token() text walk where the docs' text examples generally steer readers toward get_token_name(); get_tag() is still documented and valid after checking #tag. Execution passed 10/10 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: No hidden cases failed in any trial. The docs did well on the key distinctions: create_fragment() says BODY-fragment parsing is appropriate for chunks of rendered content; next_token() says to use token walking when text matters, warns that element text can be split across #text tokens, and explicitly notes that SCRIPT, STYLE, TITLE, and TEXTAREA have no #text children; get_modifiable_text() states that #text, TITLE, and TEXTAREA are decoded while SCRIPT/STYLE/comment interiors are raw. Those passages directly prevented the common mistakes of using the lexical Tag Processor, using next_tag(), double-decoding entities, or accidentally including script/style source. Near-misses were small: trial 3 used get_tag() instead of the more token-walk-oriented get_token_name(), and none of the trials checked paused_at_incomplete_token(); this matched the reference and tests, but tasks that require rejecting truncated input would need that check.

doc_gaps.problem: The contract is accurate but spread across prose; readers must infer which matched token kinds represent DOM text versus raw/modifiable non-DOM content.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact table listing token/current element, whether get_modifiable_text() is decoded or raw, whether it should count for ordinary DOM-style text extraction, and whether it has a separate #text child.

doc_gaps.problem: Incomplete-input guidance is present, but the special-element consequence is easy to miss: an unterminated TITLE/TEXTAREA/SCRIPT/STYLE may pause before yielding opener-carried text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short example showing an unterminated special element, the observed token walk, and the policy choice: best-effort extraction versus rejecting/falling back when paused_at_incomplete_token() is true.

doc_gaps.problem: Both methods are documented and examples use both, but the preferred choice for next_token()-based generic token walks is not stated directly.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify that get_token_name() is the general token-walk API because it covers #text and other node names, while get_tag() is a tag-only convenience after the caller has established the current token is a tag.
